title: Convergence of the real Thurston algorithm
statement: For a piecewise monotone interval map, iteratively replace its critical values by those of a polynomial with the same ordered critical data and conjugate back. Formulate and prove precise hypotheses under which the resulting maps converge, including beyond the postcritically finite case.

title: Algebraic path shifts for the power-map tower
statement:
Analogous of paths on iterated monodromy groups for iterated Galois groups of dynamical maps

Let $k$ be a field, $f \in k(z)$ of degree at least $2$, and $t$ be a transcendental number. Define $k_\infty = k \left( \cup_{n \geq 0} f^{-n}(t) \right)$, $L = k_\infty \cap \overline{k}$, $G_\infty = Gal(k_\infty/k(t))$ and $G_\infty^{geom} = Gal(k_\infty/L(t))$. \\

It was proved by Richard Pink (see \cite[Proposition 6.4.2]{Self_similar_groups}) that when $k = \mathbb{C}$, then $G_\infty^{geom} = \overline{IMG(f)}$ and for the iterated monodromy group of a continuous covering map, there is an explicit way to construct it by choosing paths between the chosen base point $z_0$ and $f^{-1}(z_0)$. \\

Following the analogous of $IMG(f)$, we know the iterated monodromy group of $f$ can reconstruct the Julia set of $f$.

1. Can we algebraically construct "nice" paths to describe $G_\infty^{geom}$ by more explicit wreath recursions? More precisely, given $z\in f^{-1}(t)$, can we find explicit endomorphisms of $K_\infty$, perhaps recursively described, sending $t$ to $z$ with nice properties?

title: Relative PCF rigidity, the necessary quotient, and a unicritical slice
statement:
regular polynomial endomorphisms

Fix $d,N$. $f:\mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ is a regular polynomial endomorphism if it leaves a hyperplane invariant, call the space of them $R_d^N$. If we restrict each $f$ to its hyperplane it gives a projection $\pi: R_d^N \to M_d^{N-1}$. In any given fiber of $\pi$ is there a curve of PCF maps? (Known: Ingram-There are horizontal families, i.e. intersect every fiber in finitely many places. There are no PCF maps above the power map).

 Alternate formulation: If you have a map from a curve $C \to R_d^N \to M_d^{N-1}$ where the map $C \to M_d^{N-1}$ is constant and $C$ lands in the PCF locus of $R_d^N$. Is the map $C \to R_d^N$ already constant?

title: Gleason irreducibility and exact critical portraits
statement:
Irreducibility of Gleason polynomials

Define the Gleason polynomials as the polynomials in $c$ such that $f_c(x) = x^2+c$ is post-critically finite.

Are the Gleason polynomials irreducible?

title: An algebraic period-three test case for infinitesimal Thurston rigidity
statement:
Algebraic proof of Thurston rigidity

Algebraic proof of infinitesimal Thurston Rigidity, i.e. if $f$ is PCF non-Latt\`es and degree at least 2, then $1$ is not an eigenvalue of $f^{\ast}:H^1(\mathbb{P}^1,\Theta_{P_f}) \to H^1(\mathbb{P}^1,\Theta_{P_f})$ where $P_f$ is the post-critical set and $\Theta$ is the sheaf of holomorphic vector fields with zeros along the post-critical set.

title: Finite ramification, critical-height envelopes, and a tame-tower obstruction

statement:
Detecting PCF maps

title: Local inertia and Frobenius in PCF preimage towers
PCF descent, higher-dimensional sparsity, and a finite-stratum certificate
statement:
Notions of PCF

$f:\mathbb{P}^N \to \mathbb{P}^N$ morphism.
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item Defn: PCF if the orbit of the ramification locus $C$, $V=\bigcup_{n \geq 0} f^n(C)$ is a proper algebraic subvariety of $\mathbb{P}^N$.
 \item Defn: ``PCF all the way down'': If the restriction of $f$ to every periodic component of the post-critical component $V$ is PCF.
 \end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}
 \item Does (1) imply (2)?
 \item Are PCF (1) or (2) Zariski dense in $M_d^N$?
 \item Is there are more general definition than (\ref{it1}) such that:

a) ``there are more of them''? (i.e. less restrictive)

b) they are dense in any reasonable topology

c) Andre-Oort property

\end{enumerate}

title: Low-period multiplier-locus conspiracies
statement:
Are there any more conspiracies?

Let $\mathop{Per}_n(\lambda)$ be the locus in the moduli space of formal $n$-cycles with multiplier $\lambda$. $\mathop{Per}_n(\lambda)$ is in general an irreducible cubic, $\\mathop{Per}_3(1)$ factors. Let $\mathop{Per}^{\ast}_n(\lambda)$ be the same but with actual $n$-cycles instead of formal $n$-cycles. $\mathop{Per}^{\ast}_3(1) = \mathop{Per}_2(-3)$ are the same line in $\mathbb{A}^2$ (Milnor). $\mathop{Per}_n(\lambda) \cap \mathop{Per}_m(\lambda')$ should be zero dimensional (need at least one multiplier outside the unit circle).

 Are there any other examples $n,m,\lambda,\lambda'$ where the intersection is not zero dimensional?

title: A canonical diamond forcing, its exact omega_3 bottleneck, and small-forcing reflection
statement: Suppose $\aleph_\omega$ is a strong limit. Is there a poset ${\mathbb P}$ of size $<\aleph_\omega$, which adds a club guessing sequence for $S^{\omega_2}_{\omega_1}$, preserving $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, and $\omega_3$.

title: Invariant Quasicircles for Rational Maps
statement: Does there exist a quasicircle $C\subset\mathbb C$ containing the postcritical set of a rational map $R$ and satisfying $C\subseteq R^{-1}(C)$?

title: Settled Quadratic Polynomials and Markov Factorization Models
statement: Is every irreducible quadratic polynomial $f\in\mathbb F_p[x]$ settled, meaning that the proportion of the degree of $f^n$ occupied by $f$-stable irreducible factors tends to $1$? More generally, does the large-$n$ distribution of critical-orbit labels of the irreducible factors of $f^n$ follow the long-term behavior of the appropriate Markov process?

title: Dense Settling and Arboreal Galois Representations
statement: For a quadratic polynomial $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$, is the image of its arboreal Galois representation densely settled? For $f=(x+1)^2-2$, determine the kernel of the quotient from the maximal $2$-extension unramified outside $\{2,\infty\}$ onto its arboreal Galois group. Also construct a natural zeta function or $L$-function for the rooted tree of iterates.

title: Laplacians on Nonsymmetric Self-Similar Sets
statement: Does a Laplacian exist on every connected nonsymmetric self-similar set?

title: Settled Frobenius Elements in Arboreal Representations
statement: Let $f$ be a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ over a number field $K$, let $\alpha\in K$, and let $\operatorname{Gal}_{f,\alpha}\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(T_d)$ be the image of the associated arboreal representation. Prove that the images of Frobenius elements are settled, and hence that settled elements are dense in $\operatorname{Gal}_{f,\alpha}$.

title: Generative Sphere Packing across Dimensions and Periodic Geometries
statement: Can one conditional generative model trained across different numbers of balls and dimensions extrapolate to larger sphere-packing instances while preserving or improving minimum separation after projection? Extend projection-corrected flow-matching methods from finite boxes to periodic packings and establish when the resulting candidates improve downstream optimization.
